content: The plaintiff sought the division of the marital home, joint accounts, and a nursery and Bed & Breakfast business. The court applied Articles 177 and 2197 to distinguish between joint and personal enterprise assets. A major interpretive problem was the classification of a B&B started during the marriage but linked to a pre-marital business. The court determined that under Article 2197, a B&B serving as a "secondary unit" of a personal pre-existing nursery remains a personal asset. However, regarding the real estate, the court ruled that the husband's formal confession during the trial—admitting the use of joint funds for the purchase—was binding evidence, granting the wife a 25% ownership share and half of the bank balance as it stood at the dissolution date.
